arml-2006-superrelay-01.title: Age equation
arml-2006-superrelay-01.body:
$3x=x+16$, so $x=8$ and Arnold is $24$ now, so $34$ in $10$ years.

**Answer: 34**

arml-2006-superrelay-02.title: Surface area
arml-2006-superrelay-02.body:
*(In the relay, $T=34$ was the answer to problem 1.)* $2\pi r^2+2\pi r\cdot Tr=420\pi$ gives $r^2(1+T)=210$, so $r^2=\dfrac{210}{35}=6$ and $r=\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $\sqrt6$**

arml-2006-superrelay-03.title: Sum of odd numbers
arml-2006-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the relay, $T=\sqrt6$ was the answer to problem 2.)* The sum of the first $K$ odd numbers is $K^2$. With $\sqrt[3]K=K^{1/3}$, $K^2=(K^{1/3})^n$ gives $n/3=2$, so $n=6$. (The values of $T$ and $K$ do not matter.)

**Answer: 6**

arml-2006-superrelay-04.title: Quadratic in a root
arml-2006-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the relay, $T=6$ was the answer to problem 3.)* Let $y=x^{1/(2T)}=x^{1/12}$. Then $y^2-y-12=0$, so $(y-4)(y+3)=0$. Since $y$ is an even root of $x$ it is positive when real, so $y=4$.

**Answer: 4**

arml-2006-superrelay-05.title: Count positions and orders
arml-2006-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the relay, $T=4$ was the answer to problem 4.)* The boys' order is forced (1 way). The girls can be ordered in $4!-2=22$ ways. Choose the $4$ positions for the boys among $8$: $\binom84=70$, but the $5$ choices with the boys in a block of consecutive places are excluded, leaving $65$. Total $22\cdot65=1430$.

**Answer: 1430**

arml-2006-superrelay-06.title: Pairing divisors
arml-2006-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the relay, $T=1430$ was the answer to problem 5.)* $K=\dfrac{576}{4}=144$. $36^3=2^6\cdot3^6$ has $7\cdot7=49$ divisors. Pairing each divisor $d$ with $36^3/d$ (the divisor $2^3 3^3$ pairs with itself) gives product $(2^63^6)^{24}\cdot(2^33^3)=2^{147}3^{147}$. So $K+x=K+y=147$, hence $x=y=3$ and $x+y=6$.

**Answer: 6**

arml-2006-superrelay-07.title: Complete the square in cos x
arml-2006-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the relay, $T=6$ was the answer to problem 6.)* $f=-4\cos^2x+4\cos x+38=-4(\cos x-\tfrac12)^2+39$. The value $\cos x=\tfrac12$ is attainable, so the maximum is $39$.

**Answer: 39**

arml-2006-superrelay-08.title: Magic square
arml-2006-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the relay, $R=39$ was the answer to problem 7 and $T=42$ the answer to problem 9.)* Let the centre be $y$ and the bottom right $z$. Column 1 equals row 2: $30+27+T=27+y+R$, so $y=30+T-R$. The main diagonal equals row 3: $30+y+z=T+X+z$, so $X=30+y-T=60-R=21$. Check: the common sum is $99$, $y=33$, $z=36$.

**Answer: 21**

arml-2006-superrelay-09.title: Tangent lengths
arml-2006-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the relay, $T=4\sqrt3$ was the answer to problem 10.)* With tangent lengths from $A$ equal to $10$ and from $B$ and $C$ summing to $BC=2006$, the semiperimeter is $s=10+2006=2016$. Area $=rs=\dfrac{2016}{T^2}=\dfrac{2016}{48}=42$.

**Answer: 42**

arml-2006-superrelay-10.title: Equilateral triangle
arml-2006-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the relay, $T=2$ was the answer to problem 11.)* The polygon is an equilateral triangle of side $1$: $P=3$, $K=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}$, so $P/K=\dfrac{3\cdot4}{\sqrt3}=4\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt3$**

arml-2006-superrelay-11.title: Rates
arml-2006-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the relay, $T=14$ was the answer to problem 12.)* Let the slow candle burn $x$ cm/min and the fast one $3x$ cm/min. After $T$ minutes: $T-3xT=\tfrac15(T-xT)$, so $1-3x=\tfrac15(1-x)$, giving $5-15x=1-x$ and $x=\tfrac27$. The fast candle's height is $T(1-3x)=T\cdot\tfrac17=2$.

**Answer: 2**

arml-2006-superrelay-12.title: Count and factor
arml-2006-superrelay-12.body:
*(In the relay, $T=6$ was the answer to problem 13.)* Each row has $2$ orders (woman first or man first): $2^T$. The men can be assigned to rows in $T!$ ways, the women in $T!$ ways. Total $2^T(T!)^2=2^6\cdot720^2$. Since $720=2^4\cdot45$, the exponent of $2$ is $6+8=14$.

**Answer: 14**

arml-2006-superrelay-13.title: Sum of odd numbers
arml-2006-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the relay, $T=32$ was the answer to problem 14.)* The sum of the first $K$ odd numbers is $K^2$, and $K^2=(K^{1/3})^n$ gives $n=6$. The values of $T$ and $K$ do not matter.

**Answer: 6**

arml-2006-superrelay-14.title: Coordinates
arml-2006-superrelay-14.body:
*(In the relay, $T=6$ was the answer to problem 15.)* Put $B=(0,0)$, $A=(0,12)$, $C=(12,0)$, $D=(6,0)$, $E=(0,6)$. Line $AD$: $y=-2x+12$. Line $CE$: $y=-\tfrac{6}{12}x+6=-\tfrac x2+6$. Intersection: $-2x+12=-\tfrac x2+6$ gives $x=4$, $y=4$. So $F=(4,4)$ and $BF^2=32$.

**Answer: 32**

arml-2006-superrelay-15.title: Test small n
arml-2006-superrelay-15.body:
For $n=1,\dots,5$ the numbers $1,11,111,1111,11111$ are not divisible by $2,3,4,5,6$ respectively. But $a_6=111111=111\cdot1001=111\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13$ is divisible by $7$. So $n=6$.

**Answer: 6**
